title: Kedgeree
subtitle: Anglo-Indian smoked haddock and rice breakfast dish
excerpt: The great Anglo-Indian breakfast classic: smoked haddock flaked into gently spiced basmati rice with hard-boiled eggs, butter, parsley, and a generous hand with the curry powder. Comforting, smoky, and still one of the finest things to eat at any time of day.

recipe.sourceNotes: Kedgeree is an Anglo-Indian dish derived from khichri (a South Asian dish of rice and lentils), which British colonists encountered in India and adapted considerably on their return home. The British version replaced the lentils with smoked fish (particularly the then-abundant Arbroath smokies and Finnan haddie), added boiled eggs, and introduced curry powder as the spicing. Kedgeree became a fashionable Victorian and Edwardian breakfast and lunch dish, served from the silver chafing dishes of country house breakfasts. It is now eaten at any time of day. The smoked haddock is poached in milk before being flaked into the rice; the poaching milk can be used to cook the rice for extra flavour.

content.text: Undyed smoked haddock has far better flavour than the bright yellow dyed variety. Poach it gently in milk; the milk can then be used in place of some of the water when cooking the rice. Add the eggs in the last few minutes to keep them warm without overcooking them. The dish should be generously buttered; don't stint.
Poach the haddock in the milk over the lowest heat for 8 minutes until just cooked. Remove and cool slightly, then flake into large pieces, discarding any skin and bones. Reserve the poaching milk.

Cook the rice in a mixture of the poaching milk made up to 550 ml with water, according to the absorption method. Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large, wide frying pan. Cook the onion gently for 10 minutes. Add the curry powder and cardamom and cook for 1 minute.

Fold the cooked rice into the spiced onion. Add the flaked haddock and the quartered eggs. Stir gently to combine without breaking up the fish and eggs too much. Taste and season carefully (the haddock is salty). Scatter with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
